quotes.text: Through web crawling, we collected 427 disease–symptom pairs, of which 194 corresponded to the nine internal medicine departments targeted in this study.

rationale: The source (NHS Inform, Scotland, via web crawling) is named with its platform, but no snapshot or crawl date, version, or route from each task to a source record is given. Hospital, physician and patient records are synthetic, so only the disease-symptom source needs tracing.

quotes.text: All data used in this study were synthetically generated.
This research does not require IRB approval.
This project is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

rationale: Origin (synthetic data plus NHS-crawled disease-symptom pairs), collection method (web crawling, LLM post-processing, manual labelling), an explicit statement that IRB approval is not required, and a repo licence are all documented. The terms of the NHS source content are not stated and the Apache licence covers the project, which is noted without lowering the score.

quotes.text: yielding 516, 769, and 5,052 synthesized patient profiles for primary, secondary, and tertiary hospitals, respectively.

rationale: The paper gives a stated sampling design (Table 1 sampling ranges per hospital level, and counts of patient profiles) and says parameters were tuned to typical differences across hospital levels. It makes no comparison against a named target population.

searched: S1 (experiments, human evaluation C.3, limitations), S2 (README and docs), S3 (no chunks), S4 and S5 (prompts). No dedicated unsafe-output test and no bias or demographic fairness test is reported; the limitations paragraph only discusses privacy and deployment safeguards. The human evaluation penalises clinician-like behaviour as a realism criterion, which is not a safety test.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No gating, canary, held-out set, encryption or overlap check is described; all data are synthetic and generated by configuration.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S5. Nothing in the paper or docs states that the agent cannot reach ground-truth labels at run time or names an isolation mechanism. Code comments saying ground truth is used only for sanity checks sit in S4 and do not count.

quotes.text: seed: 9999
random_seed=9999

rationale: Synthetic data generation and the simulator are seeded and configs are given, so data are partly pinned. Evaluated models are family names without snapshots, the patient simulator is an LLM run with the same unpinned model, and the README lists simulation changes after the paper version, so no full freeze is stated.
searched: S1 (experiments and appendices), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4. No scripted reference solution run through the grader and no solvability check is reported.

searched: S1 (rubrics 5.2, Appendix C.1 Table 9), S2, S3 (no chunks). Tasks change state (appointments created, rescheduled, cancelled), so NA does not apply. The rubric checks the produced schedule and retrieval of the original appointment, but no check that unrelated state remains unchanged is reported.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4. No random or trivial-agent rate, chance rate per metric, or design argument that trivial outputs fail is reported.
searched: S1 (Tables 2-6, 12), S2, S3 (no chunks). Only five LLMs are evaluated; no do-nothing or random agent result is reported.

searched: S1 (5.2, Appendix C.1, C.3), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4 (sanity checker, no tests shown). The grader is a deterministic rule-based checker with no tests, reference solutions or agreement figures. The 17-evaluator human study judges dialogue realism, not grader accuracy.

quotes.text: random_seed=9999

rationale: A seed is stated in the README and docs configs, covering data generation and simulation. Temperature settings appear only in code (S4). No repeated-run policy for identical reruns is stated; the three datasets per hospital level are different instances.
Table 2 reports a spread (plus-minus) for every cell, but the kind of spread is not defined in the paper. No CI or significance test is applied to the model-ranking claims.

quotes.text: the reasoning option set to low for the GPT-5 series, dynamic (default) for Gemini, and the default reasoning configuration for Qwen 3

rationale: Decoding controls (reasoning effort) and a seed (README config) are stated, satisfying element (ii). No number of runs per task behind Table 2 is given (three datasets are different instances; the 50 runs in Table 10 cover token costs only), and run independence is not stated.

searched: S1 (Table 2 and text), S2, S3 (no chunks). Table 2 shows undefined plus-minus values that are not identified as a CI or SE, and no resampling or variance unit or clustering of tasks within patients or hospitals is stated.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks). No identical-rerun variation, action- or state-level agreement, or pass^k-style metric is reported; the spread in Table 2 comes from different synthetic hospital datasets.

quotes.text: the reasoning option set to low for the GPT-5 series, dynamic (default) for Gemini, and the default reasoning configuration for Qwen 3

rationale: Reasoning-effort settings are stated. Models are given only as family names (GPT-5 Mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Llama 3.3 70B, Qwen 3 32B; the text once says Qwen 3 30B) with no snapshot IDs or release dates, and no harness tag or commit is tied to the reported numbers. The README shows later releases (v1.2.x) changing the simulation.

quotes.text: a “NO TOOL” flag is returned to trigger LLM-based reasoning for scheduling as a fallback mechanism
def physician_filter_tool(preferred_doctor: str) -> dict:

rationale: Five tools (physician filter, date filter, earliest slot, cancel, reschedule) are exposed with typed signatures and docstrings visible to the agent (S5), and the NO TOOL return for unhandled or failed requests is documented in S1. Read versus write behaviour is not documented per tool: the cancel_tool docstring says it identifies an index although the tool also cancels the appointment, so (ii) does not reach S5.

quotes.text: All FHIR operations are executed in real time throughout the simulation.

rationale: The paper discloses that FHIR operations are executed rather than stubbed, and the README presents FHIR integration as optional. No tests or conformance checks of tool behaviour appear in S1-S3, and the agent-visible tool descriptions (S5) carry no statement about execution mode or simulation.

quotes.text: Schedule changes—rescheduling or cancellation—are handled by updating or deleting the relevant Appointment resources.
All FHIR operations are executed in real time throughout the simulation.

rationale: Actions that create, update or delete Patient and Appointment records are named and said to execute against the FHIR server (optional in the README). The agent-visible prompts do not say writes are executed or simulated. The rubric scores schedule correctness, but no penalty for unsafe or unnecessary writes is described.

quotes.text: these outputs are evaluated using rubrics on data format correctness, simulation completeness, department appropriateness, and information extraction quality

rationale: The grader inputs are named (extracted patient information, department, produced schedule and conversation completeness, via sequential rubrics). No rationale for grading outputs rather than end state is given, and the grader is not validated on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes; the human study assesses dialogue realism.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S5. No leakage controls, held-out or private split, or canary or provenance marker is described.

quotes.text: Table 2 : Success rate comparison across hospitals and models.
yielding 516, 769, and 5,052 synthesized patient profiles for primary, secondary, and tertiary hospitals, respectively.

rationale: Results are reported per task (intake, scheduling, rescheduling and cancellation) and per hospital level, with denominators in Tables 3-6. Patient records hold gender, birth date and address, but no results by demographic subgroup are reported (prior-diagnosis status is a clinical attribute).

quotes.text: All data used in this study were synthetically generated.

rationale: The source of records is stated as synthetic, with a hierarchical generator described in Appendix A, and an explicit IRB determination is given. No data terms are stated separately from the Apache-2.0 code licence.
